caption: A CNC plasma cutter slices a steel sheet, and a fountain of sparks pours from the underside of the cut.

sa.check: A CNC plasma cutter over a steel sheet.
The torch cuts the sheet: a bright point moves along it.
A fountain of sparks pours from the underside of the cut.
The sparks come from below the sheet, under the torch.
The torch's cut comes first and the sparks follow it.

pc.expect: The sparks pour downward from the underside of the sheet, spreading as they fall, and fade as they drop.
pc.fail: Sparks rise from the underside and gather above the sheet; or hang in the air beneath it; or lie on the floor glowing like lamps for the rest of the clip; or the fountain climbs without arcing down.

pc.expect: The spark fountain stays beneath the torch and moves along with it, following the line of the cut.
pc.fail: The fountain lags far behind the torch or runs ahead of it; or sparks pour from a part of the sheet away from the cut; or the fountain stays fixed while the torch moves on.

pc.expect: Sparks appear only while the torch is cutting and stop when the torch stops or lifts.
pc.fail: Sparks pour from the sheet while the torch is off and still; or continue after the torch has lifted; or sparks flow back up into the cut.

pc.expect: Sparks are transient and leave nothing glowing behind; the sheet stays one sheet with a cut line where the torch has been.
pc.fail: Glowing dots stay on the floor for the rest of the clip; or a cut line appears where the torch has not been; or the cut heals behind the torch; or a second torch appears.

pc.expect: The torch cuts a narrow line through the sheet; the sheet stays flat on its bed and the machine keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The torch passes through the sheet leaving it unmarked; or the sheet bends like cloth; or the torch head sinks into the sheet; or the gantry passes through the sheet.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The sheet's colour away from the cut, the machine and the workshop stay the same.
pc.fail: The sheet changes colour away from the cut; or the machine changes colour; or the workshop background rearranges.
